# Project rules

Rules for every repo of jgolang. Global rules come from `docs/agents/foundations.md`; a rule for one repo only lives in that repo's `AGENTS.md`.

## Modules

- Each repo is one Go module, `github.com/jgolang/<repo>`, with its own `go.mod` and git history. Run `go` and `git` inside the module; never commit a `go.work`.
- Some repos hold nested modules (`log/otel`, `api/contracttest`): run the checks in each module, and tag a nested module with its path prefix (`otel/vX.Y.Z`).
- Branch from and open pull requests against the repo's default branch; it is `master` in most modules, so check it with `gh repo view` instead of assuming `main`.
- Archived repos are read-only, and modules outside the active set (see the workbench's `context/repos/`) are not changed unless the owner asks.

## Go

- Supported Go versions are the two latest releases (oldstable and stable). The core modules (`errors`, `log`, `helpers`, `api`) declare the same `go` directive, today `go 1.26.2`.
- Application errors use `github.com/jgolang/errors`: stable codes from `errors/codes`, user-safe public messages, and wrapping that keeps `errors.Is`/`errors.As` working. Do not add another error convention.
- Logging uses `github.com/jgolang/log`. Do not add another logging library.
- Tests use the standard `testing` package only, table-driven when it removes repetition.
- Before a change is complete, in each module it touches: `gofmt -l .` prints nothing, and `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...` and `govulncheck ./...` pass. Run `go test -bench=. ./...` when performance changes. Where a module has CI, it runs the same checks on oldstable and stable, and a red CI blocks the merge.
- Exported API changes are deliberate: review them with `go doc ./...`, deprecate a public name (`// Deprecated:`) before removing it, and keep README examples in sync with the defaults.

## Security

- Security is part of correctness and the project's first priority: a library is done only when it is secure, not only when it works.
- Build the minimum on the standard library; never wrap a third-party library. A new dependency, direct or nested, needs the owner's approval with its reason.
- Defaults are the safe choice: a behaviour that weakens security (a looser limit, a command-line or environment override, logging of payloads) is opt-in, never the default. A change that makes a default less safe is a behaviour change: it needs the owner's approval and goes under Behavior changes in the release notes.
- Never expose internal detail or secrets: responses carry only public messages, and logs never carry bodies, credentials or tokens unmasked.
- Treat every input as untrusted: bound its size and validate it before use.
- Pin every tool CI runs to an exact version (`govulncheck@vX.Y.Z`), and fix a `govulncheck` finding before any other change in that module is released.

## Cross-module changes

- A module consumes another only through a published tag, never a local path or a `replace` directive: change and tag the dependency first, then raise its version in the dependent `go.mod`.
- One pull request per module, in `depends-on` order (the workbench's `workbench.yaml`; for example `errors` before `log`, `errors` and `helpers` before `api`, `sirius` before `config`).

## Releases

- Tags follow semantic versioning in the style of the module's earlier tags (`vX.Y.Z`); release notes have the sections New, Fixed and Behavior changes.
- A release is cut only after its change is merged and the module's checks pass on the default branch, following the module's release checklist when it has one (`log/RELEASE.md`). Cross-module releases go in `depends-on` order.

## Issues and proposals

- Act as the libraries' owner on issues and proposals, including the `ERR-`, `LOG-` and `API-` items raised by consuming services: accept, adapt or decline each with a reason before planning it.
- Decline one-consumer conveniences, things a consumer does in a few lines, new globals, panics and new dependencies, unless the owner decides otherwise.
